text:
ava: Heads-up — pool shared-gpu-7 had a noticeable p95 jump yesterday evening, ~3x baseline. Users hitting longseqs saw timeouts. Noticed correlation with a couple of heavy tenants doing long-context rerank jobs.

jon: saw alerts too. spike window ~2026-03-16T19:12Z to 19:28Z. Any kernel flips in that window?

maya: I pulled the runtime audit logs, there's a flurry of kernel-autoswitch events around 19:13Z. Most go from light-attn-kernel -> dense-opt-kernel at batch sizes ~6-8 with seq len ~4k.

lee: that's odd — default autoswitch threshold should prefer the lighter kernel until 8k seqs. Could the fingerprinting misclassify due to padding patterns?

ava: I dumped per-request kernel fingerprints + batch shapes. There's a cluster where padding distribution makes the classifier pick the dense kernel even though compute would be cheaper on the other kernel.

jon: so a misroute causes larger kernel (higher memory working set) and that triggers KV cache churn?

maya: exactly. KV slot churn went up and we observed frequent KV eviction + reloads across tenants in that pool. With the larger kernel the slot layout expands and collisions increased. Profiling shows 40% more memcpy time.

lee: paste of the profiling snippet I grabbed:
```
# flame sample (summarized)
memcpy (40%)
attention_kernel_dense (25%)
kv_lookup (18%)
cuda_sync (10%)
other (7%)
```

ava: infra-bot: show last deploy around 19:00Z.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-16T18:47 (runtime v2.3.1) applied to shared-pool nodes: g2-family-3. No config changes.

jon: runtime v2.3.1 included a kernel fingerprint heuristic tweak, right? I remember a commit that tightened the 'dense preference' threshold to avoid tail latency for very long sequences.

maya: yes — commit 93a1 bumped the density-score threshold and also changed a fallback path when batch shapes are heterogeneous. We likely regressed for this specific padding shape distribution.

lee: action proposal: revert the fingerprint tweak for shared pools immediately and add a runtime flag to force the old decision function for pool=shared-gpu.* as hotfix. Also throttle per-tenant concurrent longseq windows while we repro.

ava: agreed. Also we should add a short-term KV soft-cap for tenants with >X longseq tokens pending to avoid eviction storms. That will hopefully limit cross-tenant collateral.

jon: I'll roll a canary with revert to 2.3.0 decision function on two nodes in shared-gpu-7.

maya: I'll generate repro harness: synthetic batch mix that replicates padding skew. Running locally now to measure delta.

lee: can we also emit a per-request fingerprint confidence metric to metrics (0..1) so we can alert if we see sudden drops in classifier confidence?

ava: yes please. Add metric: runtime.kernel_fingerprint_confidence and tag with pool, tenant. Low confidence + large batches -> alert.

infra-bot: canary rollout started: nodes shared-gpu-7-a,b now on runtime-fingerprint-revert-2.3.0. Monitoring p95.

jon: preliminary — p95 dropped ~30% on the two canary nodes within 3 mins. KV eviction rate on those nodes returned to baseline.

maya: local repro shows the dense kernel path is ~2.5x slower on these shapes because memcpy + index translation overhead explodes when slot layout expands. Strange that our earlier tests didn't catch this distribution.

lee: we should add a unit test and synthetic profile suite for padding-skew cases, and add a canary job that replays production padding histograms daily.

ava: agreed. Action items: jon -> finish canary rollback on rest of shared nodes (ETA 20m). maya -> push repro + perf numbers to the incident doc. lee -> flag metric + alert rule. I'll draft a short postmortem with root cause = fingerprint threshold regression + KV eviction amplification and mitigations.

jon: done rolling back across shared pool at 20:01Z. Monitoring shows p95 back to baseline.

maya: repro and upload: https://internal.artifacts/repro/kernel-fingerprint-padding-skew.tar.gz (contains harness + flame graphs).

lee: created alert: runtime.kernel_fingerprint_confidence{pool=\"shared-gpu\"} < 0.45 for 5m -> page oncall.

ava: thanks team. We'll follow up in incident doc with RCA and release plan for a proper fix (tune classifier + KV slot defensiveness). :thumbsup:
